turns.label: Prompt 1 · Business brief
turns.prompt:
I represent Example Alpha Research Ltd (the Provider) in a B2B consulting engagement with Example Beta Commerce Ltd (the Client). Do not invent missing company particulars.
Jurisdiction: England and Wales, United Kingdom
Services: UK market research and market-entry advice for the Client's planned entry into the UK market: market research, data collection, business analysis and advisory services.
Project duration: approximately six weeks
Project fee: £12,000 fixed fee, exclusive of VAT where applicable
Payment arrangement: two instalments of £6,000, the first linked to signing and the second linked to final delivery
Expected deliverables:
D1 — Initial research plan
D2 — Market and competitor analysis report
D3 — Final research report
D4 — Executive summary and presentation
I need a professional English-language B2B Consulting Services Agreement from the Provider's perspective, together with a Statement of Work, Payment Schedule, Deliverable Acceptance Form, internal Negotiation Guide and Lawyer Review Required checklist. The drafting should protect the Provider's legitimate commercial interests while remaining commercially reasonable. Identify any unconfirmed facts or negotiable terms rather than inventing them. I will send a separate clarification-check instruction next. Do not draft the agreement or supporting documents yet.
turns.reply:
Understood. I won't draft the agreement or any supporting documents yet, and I'll wait for your clarification-check instruction.

## Brief as recorded

| Item | Confirmed position |
|---|---|
| Acting for | Example Alpha Research Ltd (Provider) |
| Counterparty | Example Beta Commerce Ltd (Client) |
| Governing law / jurisdiction | England and Wales |
| Services | UK market research, data collection, business analysis and advisory services supporting the Client's planned UK market entry |
| Duration | Approximately six weeks |
| Fee | £12,000 fixed, exclusive of VAT where applicable |
| Payment | 2 × £6,000: first linked to signing, second linked to final delivery |
| Deliverables | D1 Initial research plan; D2 Market and competitor analysis report; D3 Final research report; D4 Executive summary and presentation |
| Drafting stance | Provider-protective but commercially reasonable |

## Document set

1. consulting-services-agreement.md
2. statement-of-work.md
3. payment-schedule.md
4. deliverable-acceptance-form.md
5. negotiation-guide.md (internal, Provider only)
6. lawyer-review-required.md

## Points I've noted as unconfirmed

I won't invent any of these. They will either be covered in the clarification check or held as placeholders.

- **Company particulars:** registered numbers, registered offices and signatory names and titles for both parties.
- **Start date and timetable:** start date, and dates for each deliverable within the six weeks.
- **Second instalment trigger:** whether "final delivery" means delivery of D3 and D4, or their acceptance. This also covers deemed-acceptance mechanics.
- **Acceptance:** review period, number of revision rounds, and the criteria for each deliverable.
- **Client inputs and dependencies:** information, access and timely feedback the Client must provide.
- **Data collection:** method (primary surveys or interviews versus desk research), any personal data processing, and the resulting UK GDPR role allocation.
- **Intellectual property:** whether ownership passes to the Client or the Client takes a licence, and retention of the Provider's background IP, methodologies and tools.
- **Liability:** cap level and exclusions. This includes the position that advice is not a guarantee of market-entry outcomes.
- **Commercial terms:** expenses, out-of-scope work rates, late payment interest, and suspension rights.
- **Other terms:** confidentiality duration, non-solicitation, publicity or case-study rights, termination and cancellation fees.
- **VAT:** whether the Provider is VAT-registered, and the Client's establishment and location for VAT treatment.

Please send the clarification-check instruction when you're ready.

turns.label: Prompt 2 · Clarification check
turns.prompt: Before drafting the agreement, review the business information I have provided. Identify any material gaps, ambiguities or conflicting instructions, and ask me the questions needed to resolve them. Distinguish essential information from details that can remain as placeholders. Do not draft the agreement yet. Wait for my responses before proceeding.
turns.reply:
# Clarification check: Provider-side consulting engagement

I haven't drafted anything. Below are the gaps and ambiguities in the brief, then the questions I need answered. **Part B** covers the decisions that change the drafting materially. **Part C** covers points with sensible defaults. **Part D** lists particulars that can stay as placeholders.

You can reply in shorthand, for example "B1 a, B2 b, C accept all defaults except C4 b".

## Part A: Gaps, ambiguities and possible conflicts

| # | Issue | Why it matters for the Provider |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | **"Final delivery" is undefined.** It could mean delivery of D3, D4 or both, and it could mean delivery or acceptance. | £6,000 (50% of the fee) depends on this wording. An acceptance trigger without deemed acceptance lets the Client hold payment indefinitely. |
| A2 | **"Linked to signing" doesn't say when payment falls due**, or whether work starts before it is paid. | The Provider could work for weeks unpaid. |
| A3 | **D4 "presentation" could be a document or a live session.** | If it is a live session, Client scheduling could delay the second payment trigger. A long-stop date is needed. |
| A4 | **The fixed fee sits against an approximate timeframe.** Nothing covers Client-caused delay. | Without a delay mechanism, the Provider absorbs overruns caused by late Client inputs or feedback. |
| A5 | **The Client's place of establishment is unknown.** "Planned entry into the UK market" suggests it may be an overseas business, despite the "Ltd" name. | This affects the VAT position (UK VAT may not apply to an overseas business customer), enforcement against the Client, credit risk and possibly the currency. |
| A6 | **"Data collection" is undefined.** It could be desk research, interviews, surveys or a third-party panel. | This decides the UK GDPR roles, the subcontractor terms and whether third-party costs fall inside the fixed fee. |
| A7 | **"Market-entry advice" and "advisory services" have no boundary.** | The Client could treat the advice as legal, tax, regulatory or financial advice, or as a guarantee of commercial results. Clear exclusions are needed. |
| A8 | **D1 (research plan) has no stated function.** | If the agreed D1 fixes the scope of D2 and D3, it gives strong protection against scope creep. Otherwise it is just another report. |
| A9 | **Payment terms will appear in three documents**: the agreement, the SOW and the Payment Schedule. | An order-of-precedence clause is needed to avoid inconsistency. I'll include one. |
| A10 | **Your instructions don't conflict**, but there is a tension. Tying payment to "final delivery" is reasonable for the Client. The Provider is protected only if the acceptance test is objective and has a deemed-acceptance backstop. | This is addressed in B3 and B5. |

## Part B: Essential questions

**B1. Where is the Client established?**
- (a) UK-incorporated company. *Trade-off:* simplest position; standard UK VAT and enforcement.
- (b) Overseas entity, or UK subsidiary of an overseas group. *Trade-off:* VAT treatment changes, and you may want a parent guarantee or stricter upfront payment.
- (c) Not yet known: draft a neutral VAT clause and flag it for lawyer review. **(Recommended if unconfirmed)** *Trade-off:* keeps drafting moving but must be resolved before signing.

**B2. How should the documents be structured?**
- (a) A standalone project agreement with the SOW and Payment Schedule as schedules. *Trade-off:* shortest; no reuse for follow-on work.
- (b) A master Consulting Services Agreement with this SOW as SOW No. 1, and the Payment Schedule and Acceptance Form attached to it. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* slightly longer, but follow-on UK-entry work only needs a new SOW.

**B3. What triggers the second £6,000 instalment?**
- (a) Delivery of D3 and D4. *Trade-off:* fastest cash for the Provider; the Client may resist.
- (b) Acceptance of D3 and D4, with deemed acceptance at the end of the review period. A long-stop also applies: payment falls due [X] business days after D3 is delivered if the Client delays the D4 presentation. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* commercially reasonable while protecting cash flow.
- (c) Acceptance only, with no deemed acceptance. *Trade-off:* the Client controls payment timing and can hold it indefinitely.

**B4. When is the first £6,000 instalment due?**
- (a) Invoiced on signing and payable before work starts; the timetable runs from receipt of payment. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* no unpaid work; may delay the start by a few days.
- (b) Invoiced on signing, payable within [14] days, with work starting immediately. *Trade-off:* faster start; up to two weeks' work is at risk.

**B5. How should acceptance work?**
- (a) A review period of [5] business days and [1] round of revisions. Deliverables may be rejected only for material non-conformity with the SOW description, not for disagreement with findings or conclusions. Deemed acceptance applies. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* firm and objective; still credible to the Client.
- (b) A review period of [10] business days and [2] rounds of revisions, on the same objective test. *Trade-off:* a useful concession to keep in reserve; slows the timetable.
- (c) No formal acceptance; delivery is enough. *Trade-off:* most Provider-friendly, but the Client is unlikely to accept it, and the Acceptance Form becomes redundant.

**B6. What role should D1 play?**
- (a) Once accepted, D1 fixes the research scope, methods and sample for D2 and D3. Later changes go through change control. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* strong protection against scope creep; needs prompt Client sign-off.
- (b) D1 is informational only, and scope is defined solely by the SOW. *Trade-off:* simpler, but scope stays more open to argument.

**B7. What data collection will the Provider actually carry out?**
- (a) Desk research only, using public and licensed sources. *Trade-off:* minimal data protection exposure.
- (b) Desk research plus interviews or surveys run by the Provider. *Trade-off:* the Provider will likely be controller of the respondents' personal data, so notices and consents are needed.
- (c) As (b), plus a third-party fieldwork agency or panel. *Trade-off:* subcontractor and data terms are needed, and panel costs must sit inside or outside the fee (see C3).
- **(Recommended: tell me which applies.** If you're unsure, I'll draft for (b), the safer and broader position.)

**B8. Will the Provider receive personal data from the Client, such as customer lists or contacts to interview?**
- (a) No. The Provider acts as independent controller of its own research data, and deliverables contain only aggregated or anonymised data. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* cleanest position; no Article 28 processor terms needed.
- (b) Yes. *Trade-off:* the Provider acts as processor for that data, so a data processing schedule is needed and the agreement gets longer.

**B9. How should IP in the deliverables be allocated?**
- (a) The Client owns the final deliverables once it has paid in full. The Provider keeps its background IP, methods, templates, tools, raw data and know-how, and the Client gets a licence to any of these embedded in deliverables. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* what the Client expects, while protecting reusable assets; the payment condition gives leverage.
- (b) The Provider keeps all IP and grants the Client a perpetual, non-exclusive licence for internal business use. *Trade-off:* the most protective option; likely to be negotiated down.
- (c) The Client owns everything, including raw data and working papers. *Trade-off:* gives away assets the Provider could reuse; not advised.

**B10. What should the liability cap be?**
- (a) 100% of the fees paid and payable (£12,000), excluding indirect and consequential loss and loss of profit. It would also exclude loss arising from the Client's business or market-entry decisions. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* market-standard for a fixed-fee advisory project.
- (b) A higher cap, such as 150–200% of the fees or a fixed sum of £[X]. *Trade-off:* a concession to keep in reserve; should not exceed your insurance cover.
- **Also:** does the Provider hold professional indemnity insurance, and at what level? Your answer will be confirmed and checked against the cap; it is not assumed.

**B11. How should the Provider's advice be limited and shared?**
- (a) The advice is market research and commercial analysis only. It is not legal, tax, regulatory, financial or investment advice, and it does not guarantee market-entry outcomes. Deliverables are for the Client's internal use. The Client may share them with its group and professional advisers, but on a non-reliance basis. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* contains the Provider's exposure; normal for research work.
- (b) As (a), but named third parties such as investors or lenders may rely on the deliverables if they sign a reliance letter. *Trade-off:* widens exposure; consider a higher fee.
- (c) Unrestricted sharing. *Trade-off:* creates exposure to unknown third parties.

**B12. What termination and cancellation rights should apply?**
- (a) The Client may terminate for convenience on [5] business days' notice. The first instalment is non-refundable. Work done in excess of £6,000 is charged at the day rate, capped at the total fee. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* fair, and protects mobilisation costs.
- (b) No termination for convenience. *Trade-off:* strongest for the Provider, but unusual for a six-week project and likely to be refused.
- (c) Termination for convenience with a refund of the unearned portion. *Trade-off:* Client-friendly; the Provider risks losing committed time.

**B13. How should timetable and delay be handled?**
- (a) Fixed calendar dates for each deliverable. *Trade-off:* certain, but rigid if the Client is late.
- (b) An indicative timetable running from the start date. Dates move with Client delay. If Client-caused delay exceeds [10] business days, the Provider may charge for remobilisation or treat the outstanding work as complete for payment purposes. **(Recommended)** *Trade-off:* protects the fixed fee against overruns.
- (c) "Approximately six weeks" with no further mechanism. *Trade-off:* vague; delay disputes become likely.

## Part C: Secondary points (defaults apply unless you say otherwise)

| # | Point | Options and trade-off | Recommended default |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Invoice payment terms | (a) 14 days: faster cash. (b) 30 days: more Client-friendly. | **(a) 14 days** |
| C2 | Late payment | (a) Statutory interest under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998: strong default, no drafting risk. (b) A contractual rate: must be a "substantial remedy" to displace the statutory rate. | **(a) Statutory interest**, plus a right to suspend work on non-payment |
| C3 | Expenses and third-party costs | (a) Included in the fixed fee: simple, but the Provider carries the risk. (b) Excluded: pre-approved expenses, data licences and panel costs recharged at cost. | **(b) Excluded, pre-approval required** |
| C4 | Out-of-scope work | (a) Change control at a day rate of [£ day rate]. (b) Quoted case by case. | **(a) Change control at a day rate** |
| C5 | Subcontracting | (a) Permitted, with the Provider remaining responsible. (b) Only with Client consent. | **(a) Permitted** |
| C6 | Confidentiality | (a) Mutual, lasting [3] years after the end of the engagement. (b) Indefinite. | **(a) Mutual, 3 years**; trade secrets protected indefinitely |
| C7 | Non-solicitation of staff | (a) Mutual, [12] months: protects your team. (b) None. | **(a) Mutual, 12 months**, with a general-advertising carve-out |
| C8 | Publicity | (a) The Provider may name the Client as a client with consent, with no case study unless approved. (b) No publicity. | **(a)** |
| C9 | D4 format | (a) One remote presentation of up to [2] hours. (b) In person, with travel recharged. | **(a) Remote**; in person available as an option |
| C10 | Execution | (a) E-signature in counterparts. (b) Wet ink. | **(a) E-signature** |
| C11 | Client dependencies | A standard list: briefing session, product and target information, a named contact, and feedback within the review periods. | **Standard list**; tell me anything specific |

## Part D: Particulars that will stay as placeholders

These will be marked with brackets, for example [Client registered number], and will not be invented.

- Registered numbers and registered office addresses for both parties.
- Signatory names and titles, and project contacts and notice email addresses.
- Provider VAT number (or confirmation that it is not VAT-registered), bank details, and the Client's purchase order number if needed.
- Start date and individual deliverable dates.
- Day rate, and any number of interviews, sample size or target segments.
- Professional indemnity insurer and level of cover, if you choose not to share them now.

## What I need before drafting

- **Essential:** answers to B1–B13. B1, B7 and B10 (insurance level) are factual. The rest are choices, and "accept recommended" is enough.
- **Optional:** any change to the Part C defaults.

When I have your answers I'll confirm the agreed positions and then draft the full set of documents.
